comments.author: @kaiandreas1990
comments.text:
"I know that sometime Finland is excluded from this specific geographic designation" 

Well, that is because they aren't included, and never have been, this is something that people outside the Nordic region have simply made up, and continue to spread misinformation about.
 
It is like saying Ireland is part of Great Britain. It is simply incorrect. 

Quoting verbatim from the official Norwegian encyclopedia: 
Scandinavia is a term for the countries of Denmark, Norway, and Sweden. 
The Nordic region consists of the Scandinavian countries, in addition to Finland and Iceland, as well as the Faroe Islands, Greenland, and Åland.

The End.

comments.author: @Natsymir
comments.text: A possible additional factor: In the 14th century, Norway was nearly completely destroyed by the Black Death. Before that, Norway was a wealthy kingdom on the rise, but it had a critical weakness - the population was clustered in densely populated agricultural areas connected by fiords, so all communication was based on sea travel. This made the country extremely vulnerable to the spread of the Black Death, and contributed to the collapse of the Norwegian kingdom and its submission under Denmark for 500 years.
